subject.title: 2026.7.1 doctor --fix hangs on large Memory Core migration with multi-GB WAL and zero committed rows

question: Should legacy Memory Core migration become a resumable sequence of committed batches, or remain fully atomic and refuse large stores until an offline migration path is available?
rationale: The current single savepoint is atomic but operationally unbounded, while naïve batching could expose partial canonical state; repository policy does not by itself choose the permanent upgrade contract between these safety properties.

options.title: Resumable staged migration
options.body: Commit idempotent batches behind a durable migration-state marker, keep runtime access disabled until final verification, and resume safely after interruption.

options.title: Offline atomic migration
options.body: Retain one atomic transaction but preflight large stores and require an explicit offline migration flow with progress and sufficient disk-space checks.

options.title: Defer automatic migration
options.body: Stop `doctor --fix` from importing oversized indexes and leave the legacy database authoritative until a dedicated migration tool is ready.

recommendation.title: Resumable staged migration
recommendation.body: Commit idempotent batches behind a durable migration-state marker, keep runtime access disabled until final verification, and resume safely after interruption.

likelyOwner.reason: They co-authored the released migration and have adjacent Memory Core and doctor ownership history.
